To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PD‐L1 expression is increased in whole‐blood cells from patients with active TB compared with whole blood cells from healthy controls or from Mtb‐exposure controls, and that this increase is largely attributable to increased PD‐L1 in neutrophils in active TB patients.
PD‐L1 expression is increased in whole-blood from active TB patients; and neutrophils are a major source of the PD‐L1 in whole blood.
PD‐L1 is up-regulated in the blood of TB patients, and this increase is driven by neutrophils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of immune control of tuberculosis, and the development of improved diagnostics and therapeutics for this important disease.
the development of a novel immunotherapeutic for tuberculosis (TB).
the role of the PD‐1/PD‐L1 pathway in TB and the identification of potential biomarkers of active disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PD-L1 is over-expressing by neutrophils of active TB patients and it is associated with disease severity.
the PD‐1 pathway may be involved in TB pathogenesis, and that the expression of PD‐L1 by neutrophils may be one of the factors that contribute to this.
the PD‐L1 expression by neutrophil in the blood of TB patients is a potential biomarker of active TB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PD‐L1 is expressed on neutrophils and monocytes in active TB patients, and this may contribute to the pathogenesis of active TB.
PD‐L1 is upregulated by neutrophils during active TB and that the PD‐1/PD‐L1 axis is a potential target for the treatment of active TB.
the expression of PD-L1 by neutrophils increases in active TB and this increase is associated with increased PD-L1 expression by CD14+ monocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PD‐1 pathway is involved in the host response to Mtb, and that neutrophils may play a role in this.
neutrophils in active TB patients have a distinct phenotype, which is characterised by increased PD‐L1 expression.
PD-L1 expression is upregulated in the blood of TB patients and that this is largely due to neutrophils, which are a major source of PD-L1 expression in whole blood.
